description: Three-panel composite of bright-field TEM micrographs of hot-rolled Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe low-density steel; each panel carries a 2 µm scale bar and white arrows marking dislocation features. (a) is the 0.5Be steel: a large, nearly featureless grain interior with only a few individual dislocations and a small subgrain/boundary junction marked by two arrows — by far the sparsest dislocation structure. (b) is the 1.0Be steel: a grain crossed by straight planar bands with pronounced dark dislocation arrangements where the bands meet, arrows pointing at localised dislocation clusters. (c) is the 1.5Be steel: strongly deformed contrast with dark, dense dislocation tangles and cell/wall structures, three arrows marking dislocation walls and their intersections. Read in sequence the panels make a single argument: as Be content rises from 0.5Be to 1.5Be the dislocation density and the coarseness of the dislocation substructure increase progressively. The caption attributes the panels to 0.5Be, 1.0Be and 1.5Be steels respectively; the citing text links the increasing dislocation density to solid-solution strengthening by Be, dispersed Be–Fe phase precipitation, and the KAM statistics from EBSD. No numeric values other than the 2 µm scale bars are printed.
measured_quantities: dislocation density (relative, qualitative from TEM bright-field contrast)

observations.observation: The figure group consists of three bright-field TEM micrographs, each annotated with a 2 µm scale bar.
White arrows in all three panels mark dislocation features (dislocation lines, clusters and walls).
Panel (a) shows the lowest dislocation contrast: a large grain interior with only isolated dislocations and a small boundary junction.
Panel (b) shows straight planar bands crossing a grain with dark dislocation arrangements concentrated at the band intersections and boundaries.
Panel (c) shows the strongest deformation contrast, with dense dark dislocation tangles and cell/wall structures.
The caption states the panels are bright-field TEM images of Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe steel after rolling, with (a), (b) and (c) being the structures of 0.5Be, 1.0Be and 1.5Be steel respectively.
The citing text states that the internal dislocations of hot-rolled steel with different Be contents are shown by the white arrows in Fig. 16.
The citing text asserts that with increasing Be content the dislocations shown in the TEM bright-field images increase gradually, consistent with the KAM chart of EBSD statistics.
The citing text states that the addition of Be increases the dislocation density, which strengthens the steel.

The citing text attributes the hardness contribution to solid-solution strengthening by Be and to precipitation of the Be–Fe phase, whose small size and dispersed distribution in rolled 1.0Be and 1.5Be steel is noted; the images alone do not resolve individual Be–Fe precipitates.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 0.5Be steel with a 2 µm scale bar; a large grain interior almost free of dislocation contrast, with a boundary/subgrain junction marked by two white arrows. Two faint straight lines (extinction contours or slip traces) cross the field.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 1.0Be steel with a 2 µm scale bar; straight planar bands traverse an equiaxed grain and dark, ragged dislocation arrangements decorate the band intersections and boundaries, marked by two white arrows.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 1.5Be steel with a 2 µm scale bar; the field shows dense, dark dislocation tangles and cell/wall structures with strong strain contrast; three white arrows point at dislocation walls and their intersections.

unreadable_items: No crystallographic indices, diffraction patterns or quantitative scale annotations are present in any panel; no numeric dislocation density values are printed
